r03.

**Premise correction**: There is no nightly database-cleanup job, and no cron scheduler is wired up in this codebase.

There is an `internal/scheduler` package (`internal/scheduler/scheduler.go`) that implements a generic cron-style job scheduler, but a repo-wide search shows it is referenced only by its own test files (`internal/scheduler/example_test.go`, `internal/scheduler/integration_test.go`) — it is never imported or constructed anywhere in `server/`, `cmd/`, or any other production code path. It is unused, dead code with respect to the running server.

The only background jobs actually started at server startup (`server/server.go`'s `startBackgroundRunners`) are the `s3presign.Runner` (re-signs S3 attachment URLs every 12 hours — see the earlier `h01` answer in this conversation) — there is no database-cleanup runner, cron job, or scheduled "nightly" task of any kind. The "cleanup" references that do exist in the code (e.g. `server/router/api/v1/user_service.go:421-450`, `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:579`) are inline, on-request cleanup steps (removing orphaned attachments when a user or memo is deleted), not scheduled/cron-based jobs.
